episodes.title: They wore WHAT on their heads??? | Garbage Cults
episodes.description:
Some cult leaders promise enlightenment. Others convince people to give up their families, abandon their possessions, eat food out of dumpsters... and apparently wear baby diapers on their heads.

In this episode of Triggered, we're diving into two of the strangest religious cults.

First: The Brethren, also known as the Garbage Eaters.

Founded by Jim Roberts in the early 1970s, the Brethren recruited young people, including students from some of America's top universities and convinced them to leave behind their families, careers, possessions and normal lives.

Members traveled across the country in small groups, hitchhiked from city to city, made their own clothing and survived largely by pulling discarded food from dumpsters behind grocery stores and restaurants.

Medical care was discouraged. Marriage was forbidden. Contact with family was eventually cut off completely. Even laughter, dancing and children playing were considered distractions from God.

And incredibly, versions of the group reportedly continued operating even after Roberts died.

Then we get into the Christ Family, led by California painting contractor Charles Franklin McHugh, a man who disappeared into the Arizona desert for forty days and came back calling himself Jesus Christ Lightning Amen.

His followers wore white robes, walked barefoot, rejected conventional jobs and also survived partly by dumpster diving.

And yes...

Some of the men wore baby diapers on their heads as headdresses.

But underneath the bizarre appearance was something much darker.

The Christ Family became connected to large-scale drug activity, criminal convictions and, decades later, an unsolved murder mystery involving a young Texas couple whose identities remained unknown for more than forty years.

Welcome to Garbage Cults.
